lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: The résumé includes a date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They are generally unnecessary and can expose personal information or invite bias.

items.says: Make sure the code or portfolio link is live, clickable and relevant.
Use a phone-number format that target employers can use.
Use consistent date and location formatting.
Verify that the expected graduation date is still accurate when submitting the résumé.
Use official degree and institution names rather than placeholder-like names on the submitted résumé.
Use official degree and institution names rather than placeholder-like names on the submitted résumé.
Avoid placeholder-like company names on the submitted résumé if the names were anonymized for sharing.
Specify whether the 35% accuracy improvement is relative or in percentage points, and identify the comparison data or benchmark.
items.because: “Diagnostic accuracy” is broad without an explanation of what was measured.

items.says: Explain how the 14% and 6% disagreement rates were calculated, including the evaluation set or denominator.
Clarify what the routing layer restricts and how signals were determined to be in scope.
Explain what “equal accuracy” means and how it was established.
items.because: Readers need context to judge whether the tool-call and latency comparison was controlled and meaningful.

items.says: Explain what the harness evaluated or enabled beyond comparing checkpoints, if relevant to the target role.
Clarify what “catching 2 accuracy regressions” means.
items.because: The wording should not imply the harness prevented releases unless it did.

items.says: The assistant-only loss-masking work duplicates the first internship bullet.
items.because: Each accomplishment should appear once.

items.says: Check the claim that assistant-only masking taught the model to reproduce tool outputs.
items.because: That depends on which messages were included in the loss.

items.says: The backlog-reduction accomplishment is duplicated in Projects.
items.because: The accomplishment should appear in one place.

items.says: Clarify how the backlog reduction was measured and what “pending-case backlog” means.
Verify and explain the fourfold GPU-memory reduction and what memory was measured.
items.because: Switching from FP32 to BF16 alone would not usually explain a fourfold reduction in all memory use.

items.says: Clarify the conditions of the before-and-after latency measurements.
“Maintained” and “adds” have inconsistent tenses.
items.because: The role is dated in the past, but “adds” is present tense.

items.says: Explain what a three-day release cycle measures and give the prior cycle time if the comparison is substantiated.
Quantify the dispatch or backlog improvement if possible, or make the operational impact clearer.
items.because: The stated benefit is qualitative.

items.says: Clarify whether Agent Runtime Suite is independent, open source or work-related.
Explain what “Owner” means.
Add a repository or demo link if available.
Verify that “Aug 2025 – Present” is accurate when submitting the résumé.
Replace the broad adoption-and-outcomes claim with a specific, verifiable contribution or result.
items.because: It gives no concrete evidence of adoption, delivery speed or downstream outcomes.

items.says: Define “working context” and explain how the 100-turn test was measured.
Explain “raw conversation grew 100x” so the comparison is interpretable.
Include task-quality or completion results if measured.
items.because: Otherwise the efficiency claim stands alone.

items.says: Explain how the 50-way fan-out was tested.
Explain how removal of deadlocks and lost tool results was established.
items.because: They may merely not have been observed in a limited test.

items.says: Link the framework or the contribution if it is open source.
Clarify the individual contribution.
items.because: It should be distinguishable from the overall project.

items.says: Name or categorize the metrics if that demonstrates relevance to target roles.
items.because: The count alone is not very informative.

items.says: Clarify what the Kendall correlation compares and which direction of degradation the evaluator tracked.
items.because: Readers need to interpret the result.

items.says: Explain how the 400-plus trials were constructed.
items.because: Readers need to judge the evaluation’s rigor.

items.says: The backlog-reduction result duplicates the Mobility Systems Company accomplishment.
items.because: The fuller version under Experience is more directly attributable.

items.says: Expand the Skills section selectively with relevant tools, frameworks, infrastructure or evaluation methods actually used.
items.because: The list is short relative to the work described.

items.says: Replace the broad “agent evaluation” label with more specific capabilities or tools.
items.because: Specific terms are easier to scan.

items.says: Put the strongest, most relevant evidence first within each role or project.
Use consistent punctuation and spelling conventions.
Tailor the emphasized bullets and skills to each job description.
items.because: The résumé spans ML systems, agents, robotics and evaluation, so relevance depends on the role.
